prompt: How do you set up architecture governance?
completion:
## Architecture Governance 101  
> “Architecture Governance” is the set of policies, processes, and decision‑making bodies that ensure an enterprise’s architecture evolves in a consistent, auditable, and business‑aligned way.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step playbook that can be applied to any size organization, from a single‑product startup to a multinational conglomerate.

---

## 1. Why Do We Need Governance?

| Benefit | How it Helps |
|---------|--------------|
| **Alignment** | Keeps architecture decisions tied to business strategy and objectives. |
| **Risk Management** | Identifies technical debt, compliance gaps, and security risks early. |
| **Consistency** | Promotes reusable components, standards, and best practices. |
| **Auditability** | Provides evidence of why decisions were made—important for regulators and investors. |
| **Value Delivery** | Reduces re‑work, speeds time‑to‑market, and improves quality. |

---

## 2. Core Elements of a Governance Framework

| Element | Key Components | Typical Artefacts |
|---------|----------------|-------------------|
| **Vision & Scope** | *Architecture Vision* document, stakeholder map. | Business Strategy Alignment Matrix. |
| **Roles & Bodies** | Architecture Board, Architecture Review Board (ARB), Architecture Office, Architecture Change Advisory Board (ACAB). | RACI charts, charter documents. |
| **Policies & Standards** | Enterprise Architecture Policy, Technology Standards, Data Governance, Security & Privacy Standards. | Policy register, standard libraries. |
| **Processes** | Decision Register, Architecture Review Process, Change Management, Portfolio Review, Issue Log. | Decision log, review templates, change request forms. |
| **Tooling** | Repository (e.g., TOGAF ADM tool, Enterprise Architecture Management (EAM) platform), Collaboration tools, Dashboards. | Architecture repository, dashboard configs. |
| **Metrics & KPIs** | % of solutions compliant with standards, Mean Time to Resolve Issues, Architecture Risk Score. | KPI dashboards, quarterly scorecards. |
| **Continuous Improvement** | Governance Maturity Model, Lessons Learned repository, Architecture Retrospectives. | Maturity assessment reports, improvement backlog. |

---

## 3. Step‑by‑Step Implementation

> **Phase 0 – Preparation**  
> **Goal:** Get executive buy‑in and define the “why” before the “how.”

| Action | Owner | Outcome |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Secure C‑suite sponsorship | Chief Architect, Enterprise Architect | Executive mandate |
| Conduct Architecture Maturity Assessment | External or internal consultant | Baseline maturity level |
| Define the scope (domains, business lines) | Architecture Office | Scope document |
| Draft a high‑level governance charter | Architecture Board | Governance charter (approved) |

> **Phase 1 – Design the Governance Model**  
> **Goal:** Build the “body” that will run the architecture practice.

| Action | Owner | Artefact |
|--------|-------|----------|
| Create governance bodies (ARB, ACAB, Architecture Board) | Chief Architect | Org chart, roles & responsibilities |
| Draft policy & standards framework | Enterprise Architect | Policy register, standards catalog |
| Define decision registers and templates | Architecture Office | Decision register template |
| Build an architecture repository schema | Tooling team | Data model diagram |
| Design communication & training plan | Enterprise Architect | Communication matrix |

> **Phase 2 – Pilot & Rollout**  
> **Goal:** Test the governance model on a small set of projects, refine, then scale.

| Action | Owner | Outcome |
|--------|-------|---------|
| Select pilot projects (e.g., a new SaaS product, a compliance initiative) | Project Sponsor | Pilot selection report |
| Conduct architecture reviews with ARB | ARB members | Review reports, decision logs |
| Capture lessons learned and refine artefacts | Architecture Office | Updated templates |
| Deploy governance tooling (repository, dashboards) | Tooling team | Operational platform |
| Rollout to the entire organization | Chief Architect | Governance adoption plan |

> **Phase 3 – Sustain & Evolve**  
> **Goal:** Keep governance relevant, mature, and linked to business outcomes.

| Action | Owner | KPI |
|--------|-------|-----|
| Quarterly governance health check | Architecture Office | % of decisions logged, % of solutions compliant |
| Governance maturity assessment annually | External auditor | Maturity level |
| Architecture reviews for all new initiatives | ARB | Review completion rate |
| Continuous training and certification | Enterprise Architect | % of staff trained |
| Update policies every 12–18 months | Chief Architect | Updated policy version |

---

## 4. Detailed Governance Bodies

| Body | Frequency | Main Activities | Typical Members |
|------|-----------|-----------------|-----------------|
| **Architecture Board** | Quarterly | Approve strategic architecture vision, review high‑impact decisions, approve standards. | C‑suite, Chief Architect, CTO, Head of IT Ops |
| **Architecture Review Board (ARB)** | Monthly | Review architecture artifacts (solution design, data model, integration). | Enterprise Architect, Solution Architects, Data Lead |
| **Architecture Change Advisory Board (ACAB)** | Ad‑hoc | Approve changes to standards, policy updates. | Enterprise Architect, Security Lead, Compliance Lead |
| **Architecture Office / Practice Lead** | Ongoing | Operate governance, maintain repository, produce reports, run training. | Enterprise Architect, Architecture Manager |

---

## 5. Key Processes

### 5.1 Decision Register

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Decision ID | Unique identifier |
| Owner | Person responsible |
| Issue | Problem or opportunity |
| Alternatives | Options considered |
| Rationale | Why a particular choice was made |
| Stakeholders | Affected parties |
| Impact | Business & technical impact |
| Approval | Approving body & date |
| Status | Open/Closed |
| Lessons Learned | Post‑decision review |

### 5.2 Architecture Review

| Stage | Artefacts | Reviewers | Deliverables |
|-------|-----------|-----------|--------------|
| **Pre‑review** | Draft architecture, decision register | ARB | Review request |
| **Review** | Architecture view (Business, Data, Application, Technology), Risk register | ARB members | Review report, approval or request for changes |
| **Post‑review** | Updated artefacts, change log | Solution team | Finalised design |

### 5.3 Change Management

1. **Change Request** – Submitted by project or solution owner.  
2. **Initial Assessment** – Architecture Office reviews scope, risk.  
3. **Impact Analysis** – Determine standards affected, compliance risk.  
4. **ARB/ACAB Review** – Decision on approval or required mitigation.  
5. **Implementation** – Execute change, update repository.  
6. **Post‑Implementation Review** – Capture lessons, update metrics.

---

## 6. Tooling Recommendations

| Need | Tool | Why |
|------|------|-----|
| Repository & Diagrams | **ArchiMate** + **Avolution ABACUS** | Unified modelling language, integration |
| Decision Log | **Confluence** + **Jira** | Centralised documentation, audit trail |
| Governance Dashboards | **Power BI** / **Tableau** | Visual KPIs, real‑time status |
| Policy & Standard Store | **SharePoint** / **Confluence** | Versioning, access control |
| Workflow & Approvals | **ServiceNow** | Customisable governance workflows |
| Knowledge Base | **Confluence** + **Guru** | Capture lessons, FAQs |

---

## 7. Measuring Success

| KPI | Target | Measurement Frequency |
|-----|--------|-----------------------|
| % of solutions compliant with standards | ≥90% | Quarterly |
| Mean Time to Resolve Architecture Issues | ≤ 30 days | Monthly |
| Decision Register Closure Rate | 100% | Quarterly |
| Architecture Risk Score | ≤ 3/10 | Monthly |
| Governance Maturity Level | Level 4 (Managed) | Annual |

---

## 8. Common Pitfalls & Mitigation

| Pitfall | Why it Happens | Fix |
|---------|----------------|-----|
| **Board Over‑bloat** | Too many members slow decisions | Limit to 8‑10 core members; rotate sub‑committees |
| **Policy Drift** | Standards become outdated | Annual policy review, automated reminders |
| **Tool Adoption Failure** | Users don’t use repository | Embed repository use in change request workflow |
| **Lack of Business Context** | Technical focus dominates | Include business sponsors in every review |
| **Governance “Tick‑box”** | No real enforcement | Tie governance outcomes to performance reviews |

---

## 9. Quick‑Start Checklist

1. **Secure Sponsor** – Get a C‑suite executive who understands the business benefit.
2. **Define Scope** – Start with one business line or product family.
3. **Draft Governance Charter** – 2‑page document: vision, purpose, key roles.
4. **Select Governance Tools** – Pick a free tier for pilot; e.g., Confluence + Jira.
5. **Run First Review** – Review a small solution; capture decision, lessons.
6. **Publish Decision Register** – Make it searchable, visible.
7. **Measure & Iterate** – Use the KPI table to track progress.
8. **Scale** – Roll out to additional domains, refine processes.

---

---

### Final Thought

Architecture governance is not a one‑time setup; it’s a living ecosystem that must evolve with your business strategy, technology landscape, and regulatory environment. Start small, prove value early, and grow the governance practice organically—always keeping the business outcome at the center. Good luck!
